title: PL/pgSQL Functions
description: Use OUT parameters, RETURNS TABLE, and set-returning functions.

data.title: Set-Returning
data.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION user_orders(p_user_id INT)
RETURNS TABLE (order_id INT, total NUMERIC)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT id, total
  FROM orders
  WHERE user_id = p_user_id
  ORDER BY created_at DESC;
END;
$$;

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use RETURNS TABLE for ad-hoc result sets.

data.title: Exercise: User Orders Function

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use RETURNS TABLE for result sets.
Use RETURN QUERY for dynamic rows.
Use OUT parameters for scalar values.
